answer: One defence is stake-gated onboarding through a single audited inlet: a new agent must lock a refundable deposit and prove sustained useful work before it can transact at full volume. Each action is signed with a cipher key bound to that deposit, so bad behaviour forfeits the stake and burns the identity history. A periodic summit of verifiers publishes revoked keys and audits the inlet. Creating many fake identities then requires many deposits, long waiting periods, and repeated forfeits, making a Sybil flood expensive while honest agents pay almost nothing beyond the temporary lock-up.
